pageText: Detect inconsistency between direct and indirect evidence in network meta-analysis. Performs node-splitting (Dias et al. 2010) on every comparison with a closed loop, and a global design-by-treatment test (Higgins et al. 2012), restricted to independent two-arm studies.
A, B, effect, SE[, study ID]
Independent two-arm studies only. Multiple rows per comparison allowed. Supply study IDs to detect repeated or multi-arm studies; correlated contrasts are unsupported.
RE models estimate shared τ² from consistency-model residuals before testing inconsistency — addresses the "FE Q-statistics inflated under heterogeneity" caveat below.
Import the shared ma-comparisons-v1 network (arm-level events/n), converted to contrast log-OR/RR for this app.

direct and indirect whiskers should overlap for a consistent network. Non-overlapping whiskers with |z| > 1.96 indicate a specific loop with inconsistency. The global design-by-treatment test is the omnibus check.
Continue this analysis with another tool

For independent two-arm studies, removing each direct comparison gives the same split as netmeta back-calculation / SIDE at a fixed shared τ². RE global Q uses this consistency-model τ² as a preset; it is not the default within-design τ² test from decomp.design. Node-splitting: Dias S et al.
2010;29:932-944. Design-by-treatment inconsistency model: Higgins JPT, Jackson D, Barrett JK et al.
